exposure: prior uterine evacuation procedure (dilation and curettage or dilation and evacuation of a spontaneous or induced abortion)
cohort: The study included 2672 singletons without prior spontaneous preterm birth who underwent cervical length screening between 18 weeks and 23 weeks 6 days of gestation.
finding: Women with at least one prior uterine evacuation had a significantly higher incidence of short cervical length (2% versus 0.7%) and an adjusted odds ratio of 2.63 (95% confidence interval, 1.19-5.80) for developing short cervical length compared to those without a prior uterine evacuation.
cross-section timing: Cervical length screening was performed between 18 weeks and 23 weeks 6 days of gestation.
gest_age: Cervical length screening was performed between 18 weeks and 23 weeks 6 days of gestation.
